R. Praggnanandhaa
Magnus Carlsen
Arjun Erigaisi
Vincent Keymer
items.explanation: R. Praggnanandhaa won the Tata Steel Masters in 2025, beating D. Gukesh in the tiebreaks after the two finished level. Gukesh was the runner-up, Magnus Carlsen did not play in the event, and Arjun Erigaisi and Vincent Keymer finished behind the leaders.

items.question: In the 2025 Indian Premier League, 14-year-old Vaibhav Suryavanshi scored a century in 35 balls for which team?
options: Chennai Super Kings
Mumbai Indians
Rajasthan Royals
Kolkata Knight Riders
Sunrisers Hyderabad
items.explanation: Vaibhav Suryavanshi scored his 35-ball century for Rajasthan Royals against Gujarat Titans in April 2025, becoming the youngest centurion in IPL history at 14 years of age. He did not play for Chennai Super Kings, Mumbai Indians, Kolkata Knight Riders or Sunrisers Hyderabad.

items.question: The G7 Leaders' Summit in June 2025 was held in which country?
options: Italy
Japan
Germany
Canada
United Kingdom
items.explanation: The 2025 G7 Leaders' Summit was held in Kananaskis, Alberta, Canada, in June 2025. Italy hosted the 2024 summit, Japan hosted in 2023, Germany in 2022, and the United Kingdom in 2021.

items.question: Who won the Men's Hockey Asia Cup in 2025?
options: Pakistan
South Korea
Japan
Malaysia
India
items.explanation: India won the Men's Hockey Asia Cup in 2025, beating South Korea 4-1 in the final in Rajgir, Bihar, in August 2025. South Korea finished runner-up, while Pakistan, Japan and Malaysia did not reach the final.

items.question: In January 2025, ISRO marked its 100th launch from Sriharikota with which mission?
options: GSLV-F15 carrying NVS-02
PSLV-C60 SpaDeX
LVM3-M5
PSLV-C61 carrying EOS-09
GSLV-F16 carrying NISAR
items.explanation: The GSLV-F15 mission carrying the NVS-02 navigation satellite on 29 January 2025 was ISRO's 100th launch from Sriharikota. SpaDeX flew on PSLV-C60 in December 2024, EOS-09 on PSLV-C61 failed in May 2025, NISAR flew on GSLV-F16 in July 2025, and LVM3-M5 carried Chandrayaan-3 in 2023.

items.question: The AI Action Summit held in Paris in February 2025 was co-chaired by the leaders of which two countries?
options: France and the United States
France and India
France and the United Kingdom
France and Germany
France and China
items.explanation: The AI Action Summit in Paris in February 2025 was co-chaired by French President Emmanuel Macron and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The United States was represented by its Vice President, and the United Kingdom, Germany and China attended but did not co-chair the summit.

items.question: The first successful human heart transplant was performed in 1967 by which surgeon?
options: Michael DeBakey
Denton Cooley
Christiaan Barnard
Norman Shumway
Adrian Kantrowitz
items.explanation: Christiaan Barnard performed the first successful human heart transplant in Cape Town, South Africa, in December 1967. Norman Shumway pioneered the surgical technique in the United States, Denton Cooley and Michael DeBakey were leading American heart surgeons, and Adrian Kantrowitz performed the first such transplant in the United States days later.

items.question: Which planet has the largest number of confirmed moons?
options: Jupiter
Uranus
Neptune
Saturn
Mars
items.explanation: Saturn has the largest number of confirmed moons, with 274 recognised as of 2025, far ahead of Jupiter with 95. Uranus has 28 confirmed moons, Neptune has 16, and Mars has only two small moons, Phobos and Deimos.

items.question: Who was the first Indian to win the Miss Universe title?
options: Reita Faria
Aishwarya Rai
Lara Dutta
Diana Hayden
Sushmita Sen
items.explanation: Sushmita Sen became the first Indian to win the Miss Universe title in 1994. Reita Faria won Miss World in 1966, Aishwarya Rai won Miss World in 1994, Lara Dutta won Miss Universe in 2000, and Diana Hayden won Miss World in 1997.

items.question: Match the awards with their first Indian recipients: 1. Bharat Ratna 2. Jnanpith Award 3. Miss World 4. Nobel Prize. Recipients: A. Rabindranath Tagore B. Reita Faria C. G. Sankara Kurup D. C.V. Raman.
items.explanation: The correct pairing is the Bharat Ratna with C.V. Raman, one of its first three recipients in 1954, the Jnanpith Award with G. Sankara Kurup in 1965, Miss World with Reita Faria in 1966, and the Nobel Prize with Rabindranath Tagore in 1913. Every other option swaps at least one recipient.

items.question: Arrange the following events in chronological order: A. Partition of Bengal B. Formation of the Indian National Congress C. Jallianwala Bagh massacre D. First War of Independence.
options: B, D, A, C
D, B, A, C
D, A, B, C
B, A, D, C
D, B, C, A
items.explanation: The correct order is the First War of Independence in 1857, the formation of the Indian National Congress in 1885, the Partition of Bengal in 1905, and the Jallianwala Bagh massacre in 1919. The Congress was formed nearly thirty years after 1857, and the Partition of Bengal came two decades after that.

items.question: Which of the following is NOT a work of R.K. Narayan?
options: Swami and Friends
The Guide
The Discovery of India
The Vendor of Sweets
Malgudi Days
items.explanation: The Discovery of India is not a work of R.K. Narayan; it was written by Jawaharlal Nehru. Swami and Friends, The Guide, The Vendor of Sweets and Malgudi Days are all works of R.K. Narayan, mostly set in his fictional town of Malgudi.

items.question: What is common to Kathakali, Mohiniyattam and Theyyam?
options: All are dance forms of Tamil Nadu
All are martial art forms
All originated in the Mughal court
All are dance traditions of Kerala
All are performed only by men
items.explanation: Kathakali, Mohiniyattam and Theyyam are all dance traditions of Kerala. Kathakali and Mohiniyattam are classical dances, while Theyyam is a ritual art form. Tamil Nadu is home to Bharatanatyam, the martial art of Kerala is Kalaripayattu, and Kathak is the dance associated with the Mughal court.

items.question: In which year were the Rs 500 and Rs 1,000 banknotes demonetised in India?
items.explanation: The Rs 500 and Rs 1,000 banknotes were demonetised on 8 November 2016, when the government announced that the two denominations would cease to be legal tender. The years 2014, 2015, 2017 and 2018 saw no such demonetisation.
